title: Transforming spinel LiMn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> into a Na-layered cathode
abstract: Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79390-z Spinel LiMn2O4 has potential to be transformed into a layered Na-storage material, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, authors investigate the ion migration mechanism during the transformation and evaluate the Na storage performance of the resulting material, including application in pouch and cylindrical cells.

title: Evolution of Near-Surface Structure, Oxidation State, and Electrochemistry of Li+/H+-Exchanged and Heat-Treated Li- and Mn-Rich NCM
authors: Tim Kipfer, Hubert A. Gasteiger and Michele Piana
abstract: Anionic redox in Li- and Mn-rich (LMR) NCMs (Li1+δ[TM]1−δO2, 0.1 ⩽ δ ⩽ 0.2) enables high reversible specific capacities (≈250 mAh g−1), but voltage and <mark>capacity fading</mark> compromise cycle life. Acid washing can mitigate these effects, through partial Li+/H+ exchange, subsequently released during heat treatment, leading to an O-depleted near-surface structure. Here, Li1.14[Ni0.26Co0.14Mn0.60]0.86O2 was washed in a phosphate buffer to avoid transition-metal (TM) dissolution and heat-treated at 120–650 °C.
